name: Fade cover
blurb: Photo, black fade, huge headline. Essay slides after.

layers.name: Headline
layers.text: Why the best accounts never post the first draft

layers.name: Heading
layers.text: Most accounts post the first thing they make.

layers.name: Body
layers.text:
The good ones don't.

They write ten hooks and keep one. They try three photos and keep the one that stops a thumb.

To an outsider it looks slow.

To an insider it is the whole job.

layers.name: Heading
layers.text: The second draft is where the post gets good

layers.name: Body
layers.text:
Cut the first sentence. It was you warming up.

Make the headline bigger than feels polite.

Then read it on your phone, at arm's length, in half a second.

If it still lands, post it.

layers.name: Sign-off
layers.text:
Save this for the next time you are about to post a first draft.

Follow for more on making things people stop for.

name: Science breakdown
blurb: Warm-washed photos, a label and a short explainer.

layers.name: Headline
layers.text: Ten minutes of morning light does more than your first coffee.

layers.name: Body
layers.text: Light reaching your eyes early in the day is one of the strongest signals your body clock gets. It marks when your day began, which shapes when you feel alert and when you feel sleepy that night.

layers.name: Body
layers.text: Bright morning light helps time the natural rise in cortisol that wakes you up, and sets the clock for melatonin to arrive later that evening, right when you want it.

layers.name: Body
layers.text: Get outside within an hour of waking. Five to ten minutes on a clear day, longer when it is overcast. No sunglasses, and never look straight at the sun.

layers.name: Body
layers.text: A window is not the same. Glass cuts much of the light that does the work, so the walk outside counts for more than the coffee by the window.

layers.name: Post
layers.text: Things I wish someone had told me at 22, in no particular order:

layers.name: Post
layers.text: Your first salary is not the number to optimise. Your first boss is.

layers.name: Post
layers.text: Nobody is thinking about you as much as you think. That is freedom, not an insult.

layers.name: Post
layers.text: Save something every month, even if it is tiny. The habit is worth more than the amount.

layers.name: Post
layers.text: The people who get lucky are usually the ones who kept showing up after it stopped being fun.

layers.name: Post
layers.text: And go for more long walks. The best ideas show up when you stop chasing them.
